narr: The remnants of TS Beryl combined with deep tropical moisture and a stationary front draped across the region produced multiple rounds of heavy showers and storms. This led to numerous reports of flash flooding, some locally severe across a roughly 50 mile swath through Chittenden, Washington, Lamoille, Caledonia, Orleans and Essex Counties.
ev: Dept. of Highways and the general public reported several roads damaged or washed out in the Richmond and Bolton areas. This was due to flash flooding after 3 to 5 inches of excessive rainfall fell in the affected area. Roads affected included, but were not limited to Route 2 by the Bolton Valley Access Road, and Route 2 in Jonesville at Jones Mill Road. Subsequent storm surveys indicated damage on Besaw Road.

Public video/picture of severe flash flooding along the Stevens River in Barnet Village. Subsequent reports from Emergency Mgmt. and NWS Storm Surveys the following morning confirmed severe to devastating flash flooding throughout the Barnet and Peacham area with numerous roads and structures heavily damaged or destroyed.

CoCoRaHS observer reported flash flooding along Depot Brook in Groton. NWS Storm surveys the following morning confirmed additional, and in some cases severe flash flooding in Groton, particularly along stretches of US Route 302. Here, several tributaries to the adjacent Wells River damaged the road, driveways and some structures.

Dept. of Highways and the public reported numerous roads and bridges washed out in the Plainfield area. Some of the damage was catastrophic with several homes completely destroyed along the Great Brook. NWS Storm Surveys the following day confirmed other road washouts not specifically mentioned in LSRs.
Dept. of Highways reported several roads washed out in the Middlesex and Moretown areas, including, but not limited to Route 100B. NWS surveys the following day also confirmed washouts on Route 100.

Dept. of Highways and the general public reported several roads damaged or washed out due to flash flooding after excessive rainfall of 3 to 5 inches fell in the Charlotte and Hinesburg areas. These included, but were not limited to Spear St., Route 116 at Commerce St., and Route 116 between VT 2A and CVU Road. Subsequent storm surveys confirmed damage on Beecher Hill Rd. and N Road.

NWS Storm surveys and follow up calls with local authorities confirmed several road washouts and bridge damage in the Moscow and Stowe areas. These included, but were not limited to Route 108 and Moscow Road.
Dept. of highways reported a few roads compromised or flooded by high water in the Wolcott area. This included, but was not limited to Route 15 near Gulf Road.
Dept. of Highways reported several roads flooded and/or damaged by flash flooding in the Hardwick area. These included, but were not limited to VT Route 16 at Belfry Road and VT Route 14.

Cabot Fire Dept. reported multiple roads washed out and damaged with bridge damage also noted. These included, but were not limited to Ducharme Rd., Blodgett Rd., Route 215, Elm St. bridge washed out, Houston Hill Rd., Danville Hill Rd. and multiple washouts along Cabot Plains Rd.
Dept. of Highways reported a few roads closed or washed out due to flash flooding in the Canaan area. This included CT-104 in Canaan just south of the CBP Port of Entry.
Dept. of Highways reported a few roads closed due to high water/flash flooding in the Bloomfield area. This included, but was not limited to VT 102 in Bloomfield.
Emergency mgmt. reported multiple streets experiencing flash flooding in the City of Barre with evacuations ongoing.

Dept. of Highways reported several roads damaged or closed due to flash flooding in the Williamstown area. Some evacuations also occurred. This included, but was not limited to VT Route 14 between Construction Hill Rd. and Business Center Rd.

Official NWS storm surveys confirmed severe to locally devastating damage from flash flooding in the St. Johnsbury Center and Lyndon areas. Numerous roads and bridges were damaged with several homes and businesses experiencing severe damage, especially on Center St. in Lyndonville where a fatality occurred. Valid time listed from initial call from public concerning flash flooding on Red Village Road in Lyndonville.

Department of Highways reported numerous roads damaged or washed out due to flash flooding in the St. Johnsbury area. This included, but was not limited to US Route 5 in Passumpsic Village and US Route 2 at VT Route 18. NWS Storm Surveys the following morning confirmed numerous other areas of flash flooding, including areas near the Fairbanks Mill along the Sleepers River, and US Route 5 over the Water Andric where severe washouts occurred and destroyed a section of the Vermont Rail System line.
Dept. of Highways reported several roads washed out in the Lunenburg area. This included, but was not limited to River Road.
Dept. of Highways reported several roads damaged or closed due to flash flooding in the Williston and St. George area. This included, but was not limited to a washout on VT Route 2A at Butternut Rd.
Dept. of Highways reported a few roads closed or washed out due to flash flooding in the Cambridge/South Cambridge area. This included, but was not limited to the Notch Rd.
The general public reported several roads closed or washed out due to flash flooding. This included, but was not limited to French Hill Rd., Route 15 and Sinclair Rd.

NWS Employee/COOP observer reported localized flash flooding in the Bolton/Nashville area after 2 to 4 inches of excessive rainfall fell in the affected area. This included portions of Nashville Road.
A few roads were damaged and/or washed out in the Waltham/Panton areas after 2 to 3 inches of excessive rainfall fell in the affected area. This included, but was not limited to East Road in Panton.

Dept. of Highways reported several roads closed or damaged due to high water. This included, but was not limited to VT-122 in Sheffield. NWS Storm Surveys the following morning revealed additional flash flood damage, some severe in the Lyndon/Burke area. In particular, several homes and a business were heavily damaged on Calendar Brook Rd. in Lyndon. Also, Hunter Farm Rd. was heavily damaged.
Dept. of Highways reported a few roads closed or washed out due to flash flooding in the Newark area. This included, but was not limited to VT-144 near the East Haven town line.
Dept. of Highways reported several roads closed or damaged due to flash flooding in the Orleans/Brownington/East Charleston area. These included, but were not limited to VT 58 in Orleans and VT 105.
Dept. of Highways reported a few roads closed due to high water in the Norton area. This included, but was not limited to washouts on VT 114 in Norton.
